newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm on U.S. rates, no records seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm on U.S. rates, no records seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares surged before trading opened on Wednesday on news U.S. interest rates were not changed on Tuesday but quickly steadied, traders said, forecasting an unexceptional market performance for the day.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened slightly higher at 359.57, up from 359.37 previously, but still off Monday's closing 366.22 record.
"That's it for interest rates -- everyone's forgotten them already," said head of equity trading at Menatep bank, Sergei Kosynkin.
"Later on when London and New York open they could come into play again, though," he added, predicting the market could rise by the end of the day but by no more than one percent.
Wall Street stocks leaped higher on Tuesday on news the Federal Reserve would leave interest rates untouched.

But analysts said the decision left open the question of what the Fed would decide to do at its next meeting in July. And uncertainty which dogged markets in the run-up to Tuesday's meeting could continue to make investors cautious, they said.

National power company UES hopped up to $0.3245 from $0.3175 at 0825 GMT on Tuesday, while metals mining concern Norilsk Nickel rose to $7.10 from $6.89. Regional electricity utility Mosenergo rose to $1.344 from $1.322.

Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin presented controversial budget cuts to the lower house of parliament on Wednesday morning, but traders said they did not expect the debate to affect the market significantly.
They said the continuing low level of Treasury bill yields would push more funds into the higher-risk equity market, helping to pad out what they said were slim volumes in early trade.
